author: Blue Spider

logsource.service: bluespiderlab_rocket.chat_proxy (Traefik v3.4, the lab's reverse proxy; the compose project is bluespiderlab_rocket_chat because Compose rejects a dot, so the container is read by name)
logsource.how: container stdout (docker logs bluespiderlab_rocket.chat_proxy), the proxy running with --accesslog=true; the application writes no per-request line at its shipped Log_Level 0
logsource.format: combined, read by det.log_event; Traefik logs a hijacked /websocket connection with a status of 0, which det.log_event's 3-digit status pattern does not match, so those 22 lines of clean.log are built as dicts with the Sigma webserver field names (cs-method, cs-uri-stem, cs-uri-query, sc-status, cs-user-agent) instead of being dropped

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: anonymous Livechat visitor registration (visitor-token IDOR)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Sees every anonymous visitor registration reaching the route; cannot see whose phone number or email address was in the body, so with Omnichannel in use it needs the request payload to separate an attack from a real visitor.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: users.listByStatus ordered by a credential field
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees the sort-order probe, which is the part of the finding that reaches the URL; the plain listing call that discloses every account's email and roles is byte-identical to the admin area's own request and is not detectable from a web server log.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: chat.getDeletedMessages called for a room the caller may not read
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees every call to the route with the room it names; cannot say whether the caller was entitled to that room, which is the finding itself, so pair it with the room membership from the application.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: downloadPublicImportFile invoked (arbitrary server-side file read)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Sees that the route was called and by how many requests; cannot see the fileUrl, so a local path and a legitimate https URL look the same until payload logging is on.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: integration management through /hooks/add or /hooks/remove
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on any use of the two management sub-routes, which is what the finding abuses, and stays silent on an ordinary incoming webhook post to /hooks/<id>/<token>; it cannot tell a revoked token from a live one (both authenticate) nor read the target_url from the body.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: roles.addUserToRole refusals (role-membership authorization oracle)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Sees every refused call to the route, which is the oracle's own answer, and stays silent on the successful grants an administrator makes; the username and roleId that were probed are in the body.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: channels.messages filtered by starredIds (star privacy bypass)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees the query that performs the bypass, with the room and the user id it filtered on, because both are in the URL; the realtime leg of the same finding travels over /websocket and is invisible here.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: anonymous write into any room through livechat/page.visited
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on every call to the route, which on a default install (Livechat off) is already the anomaly; the room id and the injected text are in the body and need payload logging.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: channels.anonymousread serving Omnichannel and deleted content
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees every anonymous read with the room id it asked for, all in the URL; it cannot show which messages came back.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: Livechat transcript mailed to a caller-named address
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Sees that a transcript was requested; the recipient address, the room and the HTML all travel in the body, so attributing it needs payload logging or the mail log.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: Livechat offline form submitted (unescaped HTML into the support mailbox)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on every offline-form submission, which on this default install (Omnichannel off) is already anomalous; the HTML in the name, message and host fields is in the body.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: chat.syncThreadsList called (deleted thread roots disclosed)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees the route, the room and the cursor, all in the URL; it cannot show which deleted roots came back in the response.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: password set through the method bridge (policy bypass)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on the changePassword leg, which names the method in the URL; the resetPassword leg of the same finding uses /api/v1/method.callAnon/resetPassword, the route the product's own reset page uses, and is deliberately not matched.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: forgotPassword through the anonymous method bridge
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on every anonymous forgotPassword call on the bridge, with the source address; the target email address is in the body.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: channels.list sorted by joinCode (join-code recovery oracle)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees every oracle question, because the sort key is in the URL, and counts them; it cannot show which channel was being attacked unless the query also names a filter.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: Livechat offline form answered 503 (mailer regex denial of service)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires when the route itself fails, which is the denial of service landing; it cannot see the long input (the body is not logged) and it does not fire on the requests that stall the server without timing out, so pair it with response-time monitoring.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: unknown method name on the anonymous DDP bridge (metric cardinality)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Fires per request on any anonymous method name outside the shipped client's own set, which is how the series are created; Sigma does not count, so the volume that makes it a denial of service has to be read from the number of alerts.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: livechat/visitors.pagesVisited read (visitor tokens disclosed)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.coverage: Sees each read and the conversation it was for, both in the URL; it cannot show whether the tokens that came back were then used, which shows up as visitor-token traffic on /api/v1/livechat/*.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: Livechat webhook test fired (server-side request forgery)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Fires on each test, which is the request that performs the fetch; the URL that gets fetched is a workspace setting, not part of this request, so pair it with the POST /api/v1/omnichannel/integrations that set it.

rules.title: Rocket.Chat: users.register refusals (account enumeration by email address)
rules.author: Blue Spider
rules.limitation: the payload is in the request body, which a web server does not log: this rule detects the request reaching the route, and application or proxy logs are needed to see the payload
rules.coverage: Sees every refused registration attempt and the source address; the email address that was probed is in the body, so the enumeration target needs payload logging.

skipped.why: NEEDS_MANUAL (the Mongo operator is a DDP method parameter)
skipped.evidence: 4 lines of 'GET /websocket' status 0; the REST sibling the writeup names (POST /api/v1/method.call/getRoomByTypeAndName) is a call the product's own client makes, and clean.log carries it

notes: Rocket.Chat is a JSON API with a realtime transport, and this is what that means for detection from an access log: of the 57 CONFIRMED findings, 20 put something in the request line that separates the attack from the legitimate use of the same route (a sort key the client never sends, a method name in the path, a management sub-route, a refusal status), and those are the rules here. For the other 37 the request is byte-identical to traffic this workspace's own client produces, and what distinguishes the attack is in the JSON body, in a header, in the response, or inside a /websocket session; each is listed in skipped[] with the line the lab actually logged and the log source that would see it. Three switches the product already ships would cover most of them: Log_Level 1 (middlewares/logger.ts:15-31, adds a per-request line with the caller's user id), LOG_REST_PAYLOAD=true (lib/logger/logPayloads.ts:5, adds the request body) and Log_Trace_Methods (server/settings/logs.ts:24, names the DDP methods). None of them is on by default, so a stock deployment cannot see those 37 attacks at all. Positives are the attack's own request lines, selected from each replay window by the regex recorded in that rule's validation log; the whole window is kept beside the rule as <VULN-ID>.capture.log, because an exploit also provisions its accounts and rooms and a rule must not fire on that. Every rule was additionally matched against the non-attack lines of its own run (same_run_other_lines in each validation block) and fired on none of them. Two routes are deliberately absent from clean.log, and the rules that rest on them say so in falsepositives: chat.getDeletedMessages and chat.syncThreadsList (no first-party caller of either exists in this build, so no client of this deployment produces them), and the /api/v1/livechat/* attack routes (Omnichannel is off by its shipped default here, so the widget that would call them does not run; the client does call livechat/config/routing, which clean.log carries and no rule matches). det.sigma_for_finding fills its own blue_spider.limitation only when the request body carries one of its attack markers (a script tag, a traversal, a SQL keyword), which a JSON body does not, although its det.observables still reports detectable_from_webserver_log: false. The 12 rules whose payload is body-only therefore carry that statement in the generator's own words; the other 8 key on the URL and carry none.
